exposure: senior supervision of trainees (supervised by a scrubbed consultant, or not)
outcome: number of procedures revised for aseptic loosening/lysis
cohort: The study included 106,206 adult patients who underwent primary unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) for osteoarthritis, recorded in the National Joint Registry for England and Wales between 2003 and 2019.
finding: The study found no association between surgeon grade (consultant vs. trainee) or the level of scrubbed consultant supervision for trainees and the risk of all-cause revision surgery following UKR, indicating comparable implant survival outcomes.
